understandable.evidence: Wells Fargo is a bank whose core business of taking deposits and providing loans is well understood [D01].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: As a large, efficient California bank, it has established a competitive position through expense discipline [D01].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: Despite cyclical loan-loss provisions, the company has maintained positive net income through the late 1980s [D02, D06].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: The bank has demonstrated a strong historical return on equity above 20% [D02].

capital_intensity.evidence: Banking is capital-intensive and inherently leveraged, and per era rules, we assess this with caution regarding credit risks [D01, D02].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: Management led by Carl Reichardt and Paul Hazen demonstrates clear expense discipline and rational focus [D01].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: With earnings in the hundreds of millions and assets near $50 billion, it is a meaningful investment for Berkshire [D02].

price_screen.evidence: Trading at less than 5x after-tax earnings, the yield significantly exceeds the 8.66% yield of the 10-year Treasury [D04].

conflicts_resolved: D02 common equity/assets ratio (5.04%) used over total equity ratio (5.87%) as it is a more conservative measure of tangible capital.
D03 recurring 1990 income used (excluding one-time gain) to normalize earnings for valuation purposes.
gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a well-managed, highly efficient California franchise capable of generating strong returns on equity despite industry cyclicality

gate2.why_available: The market is reacting to broad industry fears regarding commercial real-estate loan losses and banking leverage [D05]. We believe the market fails to distinguish Wells Fargo’s superior expense discipline and management quality from its struggling peers [D01]. The franchise remains intact and will compound value as the temporary credit cycle works through the system [D01, D02].
evidence: Customers continue to utilize the bank's services despite industry-wide credit pressures [D01].
The bank has a consistent record of high return on equity, suggesting the losses are a cyclical earnings hit rather than a structural impairment [D02].
Valuation at less than 5x earnings provides a significant margin of safety against potential credit provisions [D04].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market views Wells Fargo as an undifferentiated participant in a dangerous, high-leverage industry facing unavoidable losses in commercial property [D05].
what_must_be_true: Loan losses are confined to the current real-estate cycle and are not indicative of systemic fraud or core insolvency [D01, D05].
Management continues to prioritize rigorous expense control to maintain profitability [D01].
The bank maintains adequate capital to weather the current increase in nonperforming loans [D02].

intrinsic_value_range.low: Conservative estimate based on sustained mid-cycle earnings power
intrinsic_value_range.high: Optimistic estimate assuming return to 20% ROE [D02]

gate3.price_vs_value: Price is less than 5x earnings [D04]; margin of safety is high given the low earnings multiple
gate3.alternatives: Existing media and consumer franchises; Wells Fargo offers a superior earnings yield relative to the S&P 500 at 6.89% [D04]
gate3.downside_case: Permanent loss of capital if loan losses exceed the bank's capital cushion; current equity ratio is 5.04% [D02]
flagged_assumptions: Normalization of loan loss provisions to pre-1987 levels
Assumption that market price is reflected in the 5x P/E valuation cited [D04]

gate4.role_description: We are a permanent passive holder; we look for businesses with durable competitive advantages and strong management that we can hold indefinitely, allowing the business to compound value while we refrain from active interference in operations [D01].
value_realisation_path: Long-term earnings growth and compounding intrinsic value [D01].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In the 1980-1999 era, Berkshire focuses on investing in excellent consumer franchises and businesses that can be held for the long term; as a passive investor in a bank, we rely on management's ability to execute on their proven expense-discipline strategy [D01].

kill_criteria: Loan losses significantly exceed the capital cushion due to severe commercial property default [D01, D05].
Management abandons its rigorous expense discipline or engages in imprudent asset expansion [D01].
Evidence of systemic fraud or insolvency underlying the nonperforming loan portfolio [D05].
Regulators require capital levels that materially impair the return on equity [D02, D08].
gate5.berkshire_constraints: Must manage ownership to remain under the 10% regulatory threshold unless specifically permitted [D08].
gate5.opportunity_cost: Allocation to existing consumer and media franchises which currently offer lower earnings yields than this bank investment [D04, D08].
gate5.decider_reason: The position is a core banking franchise analyzed within my circle of competence and capable of significant capital allocation.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The bank's thin capital cushion leaves it vulnerable to a sustained, systemic downturn in the commercial real estate market.

valuation.intrinsic_value_range: Conservative estimate based on sustained mid-cycle earnings power; high end assumes return to 20% ROE [D02].
valuation.downside_case: Permanent loss of capital if loan losses exceed the bank's capital cushion; current common equity/assets ratio is 5.04% [D02].

drivers.driver: Price vs value — the company sells for less than 5x after-tax earnings against a 10-year Treasury yield of 8.66% [D04].
The bank exhibits a superior competitive position in California and a long-term record of 20%+ return on equity [D01, D02].
Management led by Carl Reichardt and Paul Hazen demonstrates exceptional expense discipline, which is critical for absorbing cyclical credit costs [D01].
The market has incorrectly conflated Wells Fargo's well-run business with struggling industry peers due to broader commercial real-estate fears [D01, D05].

kill_criteria: Loan losses significantly exceed the capital cushion due to severe commercial property default [D01, D05].
Management abandons its rigorous expense discipline or engages in imprudent asset expansion [D01].
Evidence of systemic fraud or insolvency underlying the nonperforming loan portfolio [D05].
Regulators require capital levels that materially impair the return on equity [D02, D08].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A fundamental breakdown in credit quality that exceeds our expected cyclical losses, or a management shift away from the disciplined expense-control culture that defines this franchise.
final.memo:
Wells Fargo is a bank that we understand well; it is a large California institution primarily engaged in the basic business of taking deposits and funding loans [D01]. We view it not as a complex financial machine, but as a business that, when run with discipline, provides essential services to its community [D01].

Historically, the bank has achieved excellent returns on equity exceeding 20% [D02]. Its ability to maintain profitability through cycles is rooted in a profound commitment to expense control, an attribute that sets it apart from many of its banking peers [D01].

Carl Reichardt and Paul Hazen run this business with the mindset of owners rather than bureaucrats [D01]. Their focus on efficiency ensures that the bank is well-positioned to navigate the inevitable credit cycles that confront the industry [D01, D02].

Currently, Mr. Market is fearful of the commercial real estate sector and has lumped Wells Fargo in with less efficient banks, offering us a valuation of less than 5x earnings [D04, D05]. We believe this discount is unwarranted given the quality of the franchise and the management team's proven track record [D01].

We are acquiring this business at a pretax earnings yield that is highly attractive compared to the 8.66% yield available on 10-year Treasury bonds [D04]. We anticipate this investment will provide an attractive long-term return as the credit cycle normalizes and the market recognizes the durability of this bank's earnings power [D02].

Our primary risk is the bank's thin capital cushion, which leaves little margin for error if commercial real estate losses prove systemic rather than cyclical [D01, D02]. We intend to hold this as a permanent position, though we will maintain our stake below 10% to adhere to regulatory thresholds [D08].
